title: U.S. House · New York's 5th Congressional District
area: Southeast Queens, including the Rockaway Peninsula and the neighborhoods of Jamaica, St. Albans, Springfield Gardens, Hollis, Laurelton, Rosedale, Richmond Hill, Howard Beach, and Cambria Heights, plus adjoining parts of southwestern Nassau County.

context.text: Both parties' primaries for this seat were canceled: Meeks and Marsh each advanced unopposed after Democratic challengers Frank Lozada and Salvatore Padellaro, and Republican challenger Alexandria Foxworth, did not make the ballot.
The district has a Cook Partisan Voting Index of D+24, one of the most heavily Democratic districts in the state; Meeks won re-election in 2024 with 72.7% of the vote.

candidates.name: Gregory W. Meeks
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for NY-5 (since 2013); Ranking Member, House Foreign Affairs Committee

summary.text: Gregory W. Meeks is the incumbent U.S. Representative for New York's 5th Congressional District, having served since 2013 (and previously represented NY-6 from 1998 to 2013). He is the Ranking Member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee and also sits on the Financial Services Committee.

background.text: Born in East Harlem; earned a bachelor's degree from Adelphi University (1975) and a law degree from Howard University (1978).

Served as assistant district attorney of Queens County (1978–1983), assistant special narcotics prosecutor of New York City, deputy counsel to a New York state investigation commission, and a supervising judge of the New York workers' compensation board.
Served in the New York State Assembly from 1992 to 1998 before being elected to Congress.
Represented New York's 6th Congressional District in the U.S. House from 1998 to 2013, then moved to the redrawn 5th District in 2013 after redistricting.

priorities.text: As House Foreign Affairs Ranking Member, has made oversight of the Trump administration's use of emergency authorities and its handling of conflicts in Sudan, Iran, and the Middle East a recurring focus of his public statements in 2026.

On ICE conduct: says the administration's immigration enforcement is operating "without rules, restraint, or accountability," and has called for Secretary of Homeland Security Kristi Noem to "resign immediately or face impeachment."
priorities.quote: It remains clear that ICE is completely out of control, operating without rules, restraint, or accountability—not to mention any agency coordination with Secretary of State Marco Rubio on matters related to our foreign relations.

priorities.text: On housing: supported passage of the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, saying "Every American deserves a safe and affordable place to call home."
priorities.quote: Every American deserves a safe and affordable place to call home.

positions.summary: Has repeatedly criticized ICE tactics under the Trump administration, including an attempt by ICE agents to enter the Ecuadorian Consulate in Minneapolis, calling the agency "completely out of control."
positions.quote: Yesterday's attempt by ICE agents to force their way into the Ecuadorian Consulate represents yet another outrageous and unacceptable disregard for the rule of law by the Trump Administration's Department of Homeland Security.

positions.summary: Has not called for ending U.S. military aid to Israel, but as Foreign Affairs Ranking Member has criticized the Trump administration's use of emergency authority to bypass congressional review of a $650 million arms sale to Israel.
positions.quote: Today's invocation of the Arms Export Control Act's emergency authority to bypass congressional review for two munitions cases to Israel exposes a stark contradiction.

positions.summary: Supported House passage of the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, framing safe and affordable housing as something "every American deserves."

record.text: Serves as Ranking Member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee and as a member of the House Financial Services Committee in the 119th Congress (2025–2026).

Joined Reps. Pramila Jayapal and Sara Jacobs in introducing a House resolution denouncing the Sudanese civil war on April 15, 2026, and joined Reps. Jonathan Jackson and Sara Jacobs in introducing a bill requiring a determination on designating Sudan's Rapid Support Forces as a Specially Designated Global Terrorist Organization.

Has called for the House Foreign Affairs Committee to mark up his previously introduced U.S. Engagement in Sudanese Peace Act, which would ban U.S. arms sales to any country supplying the warring parties in Sudan and mandate a comprehensive U.S. strategy to end the conflict.

Issued a statement March 6, 2026 criticizing the Trump administration's invocation of Arms Export Control Act emergency authority to bypass congressional review for over 20,000 bombs (valued at more than $650 million) sold to Israel.

Issued a statement January 28, 2026 condemning an attempted entry by ICE agents into the Ecuadorian Consulate in Minneapolis without permission, calling it a violation of diplomatic protections and international agreements.

summary.text: George Marsh is the Republican and Queens United Party candidate challenging incumbent Rep. Gregory Meeks in NY-5. He advanced to the general election unopposed after the Republican primary was canceled. Ballotpedia and other election trackers report no detailed biography, campaign platform, or public statements for Marsh, and he has raised no reported campaign funds as of the most recent FEC filing period covered.
